children.value: Medical tests for diseases are sometimes characterised by their

. The sensitivity of the test is the probability that a diseased person will show a positive test result (a correct positive). The specificity of a test is the probability that a healthy person will show a negative result (a correct negative). Both sensitivity and specificity are conditional probabilities.
